speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The combination of markedly elevated AST/ALT, high bilirubin, and recent high-risk sexual behavior suggests acute hepatitis, possibly viral or toxin-induced. Given his history of cocaine and ecstasy use, did you experience any seizures, confusion, or severe muscle pain before this illness started?

REQUEST TEST: Creatine_Phosphokinase (CPK)
REQUEST TEST: Acetaminophen_level

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Liver Injury due to Methylene Blue Overdose

Given the negative viral panel, lack of rhabdomyolysis, and your history of ecstasy use, the clinical picture strongly points to Methylene Blue toxicity. This drug can cause severe, potentially fatal acute cholestatic jaundice when overdosed. Are you currently taking any prescription medications or herbal supplements, and have you had any recent surgeries or exposure to blue dyes?
